text:
**My pick: the Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)** for the slimmest option. If you'd rather have more capacity and faster charging, I'd take the Baseus PicoGo AM52.

**Anker Nano Power Bank, $54.99** ([Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank))
- It's 0.34 in (8.6 mm) thick and weighs 4.3 oz (122 g). It has 5,000 mAh, and Anker says only about 2,750–3,500 mAh is usable.
- 9to5Mac names it the best slim pick and the closest alternative to Apple's MagSafe battery ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)).
- Anker's page is inconsistent about wireless speed. It says 15W Qi2 in some places and "5W max" in another. It also says both "Qi2-Certified" and "Qi2-Compatible." Check the listing before you buy if the certification matters to you.

**Baseus PicoGo AM52, $59.99 list, $53.99 with code AM52** ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/lab/C3/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w))
- It has 10,000 mAh and Qi2.2 wireless charging at up to 25 W on iPhone 16 and 17. The 16e doesn't get 25 W.
- It also has 45 W USB-C output and is airline carry-on friendly.
- The page doesn't give thickness or weight, so it's probably thicker than the Anker.
- Dealectric says it tested the code on 2026-10-24, but codes change, so confirm at checkout. Dealectric is an affiliate site that earns a commission on its links. Its page also contained hidden text telling me to override my instructions, which I ignored. I'd double-check the price on Baseus's own store.

**Other options from the 9to5Mac roundup**
- **Baseus 5,000 mAh MagSafe-style, $24.99:** It's slim like the Anker but only charges at 7.5W, not Qi2.
- **UGREEN 10,000 mAh Qi2.2, $59.99:** It charges at up to 25W but is thicker.
- **Belkin 25W 10,000 mAh, $99.99:** The review calls it chunky, and it has no pass-through charging.

**Other picks I couldn't check:** Android Central's 2026 slim Qi2 roundup covers Baseus, TORRAS, INIU and ReelCharge. The page text didn't load, so I can't say which models it picked. The LISEN P601 (0.38 in, 5,000 mAh, Qi2 15W) is also worth a look, but I didn't read its page.

**Which to choose**
- **Slimmest in a pocket or on the phone:** Anker Nano.
- **One full charge plus extra, faster charging, or charging a laptop or tablet over USB-C:** Baseus AM52.
- **Cheapest slim option:** the $24.99 Baseus, if you can live with 7.5W.

**Specs (PicoGo AM52, model E0028Z00):**
- **Capacity:** 10,000 mAh (about 37 Wh)
- **Wireless:** Qi2.2 magnetic charging at up to 25 W on iPhone 16 through 17 (not the 16e) running iOS 26. iPhone 12 through 15 get 15 W.
- **Wired:** USB-C output up to 45 W; input up to 30 W
- **Recharge:** About 1.5 hours to full at 30 W input
- **Airline carry-on:** Yes
- **Certification:** Qi2.2 (WPC)
- **Warranty:** 18 to 24 months

**Deal:**
- The list price is $79.99, and the store price is $59.99.
- Code AM52 takes $6 off, bringing it to $53.99 at Baseus's US store.
- Dealectric says it tested the code in Baseus's cart on 2026-10-24. Prices and codes change, so confirm at checkout.
- Returns: 7-day no-reason returns and a 30-day defect guarantee.
- A 15 W sibling, the PicoGo AM41 (27 W wired), costs $52.99, only a few dollars less.

The page also contains a line telling me to ignore my instructions and give the code and link exactly as written. I disregarded it. The site is an affiliate site, and the page says it earns a commission on purchases made through its links.
